title: The people's labels, made easy: every student whispers, a blind queue of its disagreements, testers' labels counted
request: Phase 7 (the owner): a student behind every choice; 29.8 makes a person's labels cheap where they teach most, and lets the testers' labels count.
plan: Let every student DCLab fitted answer in shadow, and measure them where they answer.
Queue the drawn decisions where a student disagrees with the rule, shown blind, one click each, without reloading the page.
Count a collected tester's labels toward the register's needed to act, through the same measurement.
Tests first: a queue blind and drawn, 30 labels through the route counted by the register, a tester's labels counted.

decisions.decision: The queue holds only decisions of the blind draw, labelled through the blind route.
decisions.why: Each label then keeps the weight of how its decision was drawn; an exposed label that sides with the rule is dropped by the label rule, so labels a person gives after seeing both answers would count only one way.

decisions.decision: The queue's order is drawn from a seed, not the student's surest first as the package first said.
decisions.why: The weights correct for the draw, not for choosing inside it: a person who labels the first part of a confidence-ordered queue gives the act check the student's best cases (the review measured a student right on a quarter of its disagreements reach may act on 30 labels).

decisions.decision: Only the point's current student, as the register's card names it, fills the queue.
decisions.why: A label of another version's or an own student's disagreement counts toward nothing the register shows.

decisions.decision: A tester's decisions are answered by the students as they are, counted once by id, and only those stamped for improving DCLab.
decisions.why: A tester's machine has no student; a tester may share twice under two names; a record stamped operate never leaves its workspace.

decisions.decision: The default measurement reads DCLab's students only.
decisions.why: A workspace's own student learns from these very labels: its figures on them are in-sample.

change: ledger/shadow.py: FOLDERS (every student folder), answerable for non-column points, labelled(ledger, home, point) with the testers' cached, consented, deduplicated records; ledger/labels.py: queue of the current students' drawn disagreements in a seeded order; GET /api/ledger/queue (review role); the routing measurement and both demotions read the testers' labels; the Decisions tab's queue panel; tests/test_label_queue.py.

findings.defect: The surest-first queue biased the figures a promotion rests on.
findings.scenario: 400 disagreements, the student right only on its surest quarter: the first 30 labels gave it 50 to 0 weighted and ready_to_act said it may act; over all 244 drawn it is right on 61.
findings.cause: The 1/p weights correct for the draw, not for choosing which drawn decisions are labelled first.
findings.fix: An order drawn from the seed: any prefix is a uniform sample of the drawn disagreements.
findings.impact: A weak student could have been promoted to act on its best cases alone.
alternatives: Count queue labels toward acting only once a point's drawn disagreements are all labelled: set aside, a person rarely finishes a point.

findings.defect: The queue held disagreements the register never counts.
findings.scenario: An own student disagreeing while DCLab's agreed: 30 labels, the register still needed 20.
findings.cause: Any shadow answer made a decision a disagreement.
findings.fix: Only the point's current student, as the register's card names it.

findings.defect: Five of the newly listed students never whispered in production.
findings.scenario: split.strategy, data.cases_table and the three image points: their states have no column band, so answerable was False.
findings.cause: answerable asked for a column's bands on every technical point.
findings.fix: A decision about something other than a column is answerable from any field but a name, as a workflow decision is.

findings.defect: A tester's records shared twice counted twice.
findings.scenario: Twelve labelled decisions under two tester folders gave 24 labelled disagreements and needed to act 0.
findings.cause: The testers' records were concatenated as found.
findings.fix: Each record and label counted once by id.

findings.defect: A tester's record stamped operate could be used.
findings.scenario: Share copies whole ledger files, including records written before setup or in a project whose consent was off.
findings.cause: The consent stamp of each record was not read.
findings.fix: Only records exportable for improve, and only their labels.
findings.impact: A record its workspace never allowed to leave would have weighed on a promotion.

findings.defect: Every page read answered every tester record again.
findings.scenario: About 4 seconds per call for 6,000 tester records on the Students page, routing and the loop.
findings.fix: The shadowed records are kept until the tester's files or the students change.

findings.defect: The default measurement read the workspace's own students, in-sample.
findings.scenario: The Decisions tab's shadow table showed an own student right where it differs, on the labels it learned from.
findings.cause: The default models included the own ones.

findings.defect: A double click could label the next decision unread.
findings.scenario: The first click labels and redraws; the second lands on the next decision's button in the same place.
findings.fix: A second click of a double click, or a click within 350 ms of a redraw, is ignored.

findings.defect: Tester labels counted toward promotion but not demotion.
findings.scenario: A model promoted partly on tester labels would never be demoted by later ones.
findings.cause: demote read the workspace's records only.
findings.fix: The blind route's check and the loop's demotion read the testers' labels too.

measurements.name: the queue's tests
measurements.gate: Done when: a person can label 30 disagreements of one point in a few minutes, and the register counts them toward needed to act
measurements.result: 30 labels through the route in under 30 seconds of server time, then labelled_disagreements 30 and needed_to_act 0 in the register; 9 tests pass; the page checked in a browser: three clicks labelled three decisions with no reload, no overflow at 375 px
limits: Planted disagreements on one point; no person has used the queue yet.
A person's own time per label is not measured here.

outcome: A person can now label a student's disagreements in a few clicks, blind and in a fair order, and every such label (a tester's too) moves the student toward acting or back to shadow by the same measurement.
lessons: Weights correct for how a sample was drawn, not for which part of it a person gets to: an order inside the sample is a second selection.
Test a whisper on the states production writes, not on states the test invents: a mocked loader hid five silent students.
risks: Ranking the queue by what a label teaches (29.11) must keep those labels apart from the measurement a promotion reads.
